findings.summary: The 'exactly one bounded rerun' property is per arrival batch; successive saves during a run produce sequential bounded reruns, which is the documented coalescing behavior.
findings.detail: The RunAsync do/while sets servedVersion to the latest requested version after each run, so any request arriving during a run is served by one rerun. If further saves arrive during that rerun, another rerun occurs. There is still at most one in-flight run and at most one pending request slot (SemaphoreSlim(0,1)), so no unbounded queue can grow. The worker's known_limitations records this and the test asserts exactly two invocations for eight requests during a single blocked run.
findings.recommended_action: No change required; behavior is bounded and matches the documented coalescing semantics.

Save response non-blocking: code path is O(1) Interlocked.Increment + SemaphoreSlim.Release; empirically confirmed the loop continuation is not inlined on the save thread, and the dedicated test proves the save returns while the enumeration is blocked.
falsification_attempts: Attempted to falsify the non-blocking claim by testing whether SemaphoreSlim.Release resumes the awaiting async loop inline on the releasing thread; result: NOT inline (afterAwaitThread != releaseThread), so the save thread cannot run CountCandidates/EnumerateCandidates synchronously.
Attempted to find an unbounded-queue path: the loop holds at most one semaphore slot and one in-flight run; repeated requests only advance a version counter, so no queue can grow.

Attempted to find a lost-request race between Interlocked.Increment and SemaphoreSlim.Release/SemaphoreFullException: the version counter is incremented before Release, so a coalesced request is always observed by the version comparison; no lost request found.

Attempted to find a stale-hint path: LibraryReconciliationService builds hints with snapshot.ConfigurationVersion read at run start, and the rerun rereads the snapshot, so the latest replaced version is observed.

notes: APPROVED. The implementation satisfies the task objective and acceptance criterion (a successful save triggers a bounded, non-blocking reconciliation that enqueues fresh work at the new snapshot version so existing posters re-render). Boundedness is structurally guaranteed (single in-flight run, one-slot semaphore, version-based coalescing, bounded shutdown), the save path contains all trigger failures, and the host coupling is confined to the implementation behind a Jellyfin-free interface. Tests are genuine and non-vacuous and drove the real Plugin.UpdateConfiguration override and the real ConfigurationReconciliationTrigger.
